prompt: The PICs are remapped to master offset 32 and slave offset 40, and the PIT is clocked at 1,193,182 Hz. You want a 250 Hz tick.

trace.label: Where must the EOI (`0x20`) be written after handling IRQ 11?
choices: Slave command port, then master command port

trace.label: Without any EOI, what happens to timer interrupts?
choices: Ticks keep arriving at half speed
One tick arrives, then IRQ 0 is blocked
Nothing changes, the PIT re-raises the line

explain: 1193182 / 250 = 4772.7, truncated to 4772 = 0x12A4, so the low byte 0xA4 goes to port 0x40 first and 0x12 second (after command 0x36 on port 0x43). The PIC adds the IRQ number to its offset: slave IRQ 11 is line 3 of the slave, 40 + 3 = 43. An IRQ from the slave must be acknowledged on the slave and then the master, since the master also has IRQ 2 (the cascade) in service. Until EOI, the PIC keeps that line in service and blocks it and everything of lower priority, so a missing EOI gives exactly one tick.
